Posterior of the event proportions under the blinded binomial model

Source: R/binbeta_post.R
binbeta_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of the proportions of subjects with the event on study drug and control under the Bayesian hierarchical model of Ball and Schnell (2016), from the blinded number of enrolled subjects and the number of subjects with the event.

Usage

binbeta_post(
  y,
  n,
  k = 1,
  prior_c,
  prior_d,
  p0 = NULL,
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Number of subjects with the event (non-negative integer).

n

Number of enrolled subjects (positive integer, at least y).

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to control (k:1).

prior_c

Shape parameters c(a, b) of the Beta prior of the control proportion.

prior_d

Shape parameters c(c, d) of the Beta prior of the study drug proportion.

p0

Optional critical value of the study drug proportion (the maximum acceptable proportion).

rr0

Critical value of the ratio of the proportions, used for the signal when p0 is NULL.

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible intervals.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles are not computed (they are NA).

control

List of settings of the numerical integration, as in exptime_post.

Value

An object of class bssd_post as described in exptime_post, with model "BINBETA", the control and study drug proportions theta_c and theta_d, and their ratio rr in place of the rates and the rate ratio.

Details

With \(N\) enrolled subjects of whom \(Z\) had the event, the model is $$M_c \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(N, 1 / (k + 1)), \quad Y_c \mid M_c \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(M_c, \theta_c), \quad Y_d \mid M_c \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(N - M_c, \theta_d),$$ $$Z = Y_c + Y_d, \quad \theta_c \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a, b), \quad \theta_d \sim \mathrm{Beta}(c, d).$$ Under simple randomization each subject is on control with probability \(1 / (k + 1)\), so \(Z \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(N, \pi)\) with \(\pi = (\theta_c + k \theta_d) / (k + 1)\), and the posterior is two-dimensional. It is integrated numerically on the coordinates \(\mathrm{logit}(\theta_c)\) and the prior distribution function of \(\theta_d\) as in exptime_post. When \(a < 1\) or \(b < 1\), the prior density of \(\mathrm{logit}(\theta_c)\) decreases slowly in a tail, which the blinded data do not bound, and \(z_c = \Phi^{-1}(F_c(\theta_c))\), where \(F_c\) is the prior distribution function of \(\theta_c\), is used instead. For \(rr_0 > 1\), the Gauss-Legendre rule over the first coordinate is split at \(\theta_c = 1 / rr_0\), where the posterior probability of the ratio has a kink because \(\theta_d \le 1\). When \(a \le 1\), the posterior density of \(\theta_c\) near 0 is proportional to the prior density, and the posterior mean of the ratio is infinite (Inf).

When p0 is given, a signal is declared when \(P(\theta_d > p_0 \mid Z) > \) cutoff (the rule of Ball and Schnell, 2016); otherwise the ratio \(\theta_d / \theta_c\) is tested against rr0. With a single study, the likelihood is that of the model of Goren et al. (2020), see multibin_post.

References

Ball, G. and Schnell, P. M. (2016). Blinded safety signal monitoring for the FDA IND reporting final rule. In J. Lin et al. (eds.), Statistical Applications from Clinical Trials and Personalized Medicine to Finance and Business Analytics, ICSA Book Series in Statistics, 201–209. Springer, Cham. doi:10.1007/978-3-319-42568-9_17

See also

signal_count for the largest acceptable number of subjects with the event, canary_post for the model with fixed arm sizes of Gould and Wang (2017).

Examples

# 40 of 300 subjects with the event, randomization 1:1, control prior from
# 30 of 300 historical control subjects, vague prior for study drug
fit <- binbeta_post(y = 40, n = 300, k = 1, prior_c = c(31, 271),
                    prior_d = c(1, 1), p0 = 0.15)
fit
#> Model: BINBETA 
#> Tested quantity: proportion theta_d of study drug
#> P(theta_d > 0.15 | data) = 0.6615
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of rr: mean 1.724, median 1.652, 95% interval (0.7135, 3.151)
#> Posterior of theta_d: mean 0.1689, median 0.1677, 95% interval (0.08793, 0.2566)
